newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-DETTORI WINS LEGER FOR SECOND YEAR IN SUCCESSION.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-DETTORI WINS LEGER FOR SECOND YEAR IN SUCCESSION.

text.p: Champion jockey Frankie Dettori won the English St Leger horse racing classic for the second year in succession on Saturday, partnering 8-1 chance Shantou to a neck victory over 2-1 favourite Dushyantor.
The result was a reverse of Epsom Derby form in June when Dushyantor, second to Shaamit, finished just ahead of third placed Shantou.
Going into the final two furlongs (400 metres) of Saturday's long-distance classic, Dushyantor and Pat Eddery looked sure to justify backers' confidence.
But Shantou, trained by John Gosden, wore the favourite down in the final 50 metres to land the $271,500 first prize for winning owner Sheikh Mohammmed of Dubai.
It was a first British classic success for Gosden, who is based at Newmarket. Dettori won the race in 1995 on Classic Cliche.
Samraan, a 28-1 outsider ridden by John Carroll, ran on to finish four lengths away in third with 5-1 second favourite Mons back in fourth.
Mons, ridden by young Spaniard Oscar Urbina, had made much of the running in the 2.9 km test with Sharaf Kabeer and Wilawander also racing prominently.
Eddery was content to lob along towards the rear of the 11-strong field and seemed to be going very easily halfway up the long Doncaster straight.
The rest of the opposition was swiftly dispatched and it looked like Eddery was set for another classic success as they approached the final furlong.
But under the strongest driving, Dettori, low in the saddle forced Shantou through on the outside for a memorable triumph.
In typical style he punched the air after passing the winning post and produced his customary flying dismount in the unsaddling enclosure.
A delighted Gosden said: "I am not sure anyone else but Frankie would have won on him. The horse only runs for him."
Dettori said: "This race really meant a lot for me -- probably equal to the Derby. I wanted to win it for John so much and the horse was in perfect nick.
"The full credit goes to the whole yard which has had a frustrating year. John's record speaks for itself. He proved it today, if he gets the right horse he can produce them on the day."
Gosden said: "That's how you want the race to turn out. It was a thrilling finish, but what a ride from Frankie."
Shantou has probably run his last race this year but Dushyantor could now contest the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe.
Trainer Henry Cecil said: "He did everything right and had the race won a furlong out but he just died in the final 50 yards.
"It's not the end of the world that he didn't quite stay. As long as he's well we'll go for the Arc."
